newsitem.title: GERMANY: Holiday mood means weak start for German shares.
newsitem.headline: Holiday mood means weak start for German shares.

text.p: German shares started floor trade weaker on Monday -- their last day of trading before a three-day Christmas break -- as the holiday season kept activity markedly low.
The 30-share DAX index was down 8.92 points at 2,845.53 after about a half-hour of floor trade, but was some 10 points ahead of its level at the close of late electronic dealings on Friday.
Activity was so thin that no official price could be calculated for the IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day electronic trade, until minutes before the floor session started.
"We should have given ourselves today off as a Christmas present," said a Duesseldorf dealer.
The futures market was somewhat more active, with the March DTB DAX future up 11.5 points at 2,864.5. The December contract expired last week.
Early movers on the cash market included Commerzbank AG, which was down 40 pfennigs at 38.80. The stock has been pushed up in the past few weeks on renewed takeover speculation.
However there was little fresh news to move the market and, with the bourse due to close Tuesday through Thursday for the Christmas break, thin volumes were seen continuing Friday.
The earliest chance of some real activity, one dealer said, was next Monday, the last trading day of 1996.
